stem:
The diagram shows Yash's triangular dot pattern with rows of 1, then 2, then 3 dots, and a square 3-by-3 dot array.

Which claim connects the triangular pattern to the square pattern?

options.text: Two adjacent triangular totals join into a square: $3+6=9$, matching the 3-by-3 array.
The whole display is only a square-number pattern, so the triangular rows need no role.
The square 3-by-3 array is what creates the triangular rows of 1, 2, and 3 dots.
The answer is 9 only because 9 is the largest count printed beside the arrays.

teacher.key_rationale: Adjacent triangular totals 3 and 6 make the square total 9, so the triangular pattern builds the related square array. Calling everything a square number swaps the label. Saying the square creates the triangular rows reverses the relation. Choosing 9 for its printed size is a surface grab.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote right-triangle source into triangular and square dot arrays; stem refers to the diagram.
